source: The city of Zamboanga recorded its hottest day in a decade on April 18, when temperatures reached 38.4 degrees Celsius, according to weather bureau PAGASA. The heat index, which measures how hot it feels, climbed to 46 degrees, putting the city in the danger category for heat stroke. The city health office reported 37 cases of heat-related illness within a single week, mostly among construction workers and market vendors. Schools were told to hold classes in the early morning, and public parks were opened as cooling spots. Residents were urged to drink at least eight glasses of water daily and avoid outdoor activities between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m.
target_summary: Zamboanga hit 38.4 degrees Celsius, its hottest in a decade.

source: A group of 12 mountaineers from Cebu successfully climbed Mount Kitanglad in Bukidnon over the weekend to plant 300 native tree seedlings along the trail. The climb, which started at 5 a.m. at the Intavas trailhead, took the team seven hours to reach the summit at 2,899 meters. The seedlings, including molave, narra, and bagtikan, were provided by a forestry office, and each was marked with a tag so rangers can monitor its growth. The project is part of a campaign to restore areas of the mountain damaged by logging and fire in the past decade. The group leader, Marco Dizon, said that members paid for their own food and transport. Rangers said that about 60 percent of previously planted seedlings survived.
target_summary: Twelve Cebu mountaineers planted 300 native seedlings on Mount Kitanglad.

source: Western music is built from twelve different notes that repeat in higher and lower pitches, and the distance between each note and the next is called a semitone. A major scale uses seven of these notes, following a pattern of whole step, whole step, half step, whole step, whole step, whole step, half step; starting on C gives the white keys on a piano, C, D, E, F, G, A, and B. The speed of music is its tempo, measured in beats per minute, where 60 beats per minute equals one beat each second. Musicians commonly tune their instruments to the note A above middle C, which vibrates 440 times per second. When several notes sound together, they form a chord, and the most basic chords have three notes.
target_summary: Music uses twelve notes, and major scales follow a fixed step pattern.

source: Washing hands with soap is one of the simplest and most effective ways to prevent infections. The World Health Organization advises scrubbing all surfaces of the hands, including the backs, between the fingers, and under the nails, for at least 20 seconds before rinsing with clean water. Hands should be washed before eating or preparing food, after using the toilet, after coughing or sneezing, and after touching garbage. Studies show that regular handwashing with soap can reduce diarrhea-related illness by about 30 percent and respiratory infections by roughly 20 percent. When soap and water are not available, an alcohol-based hand rub containing at least 60 percent alcohol is a good alternative. Global Handwashing Day is observed every October 15.
target_summary: Washing hands with soap for 20 seconds prevents many infections.

source: Sari-sari stores are small neighborhood shops found on nearly every street in the Philippines. Usually run from the front room of a family home, they sell items in tiny quantities, such as a single cigarette, a sachet of shampoo, or a cup of cooking oil, so that low-income customers can buy only what they need for the day. The name means variety in Tagalog. Many owners allow trusted neighbors to buy on credit, recording the debts in a notebook, a system called utang. Industry surveys estimate that there are over one million sari-sari stores nationwide, and they account for a large share of all grocery sales. Large companies depend on them to distribute products to remote areas where supermarkets do not exist.
target_summary: Sari-sari stores are neighborhood shops selling goods in tiny quantities.

The name means variety in Tagalog. Many owners allow trusted neighbors to buy on credit, recording the debts in a notebook, a system called utang. Industry surveys estimate that there are over one million sari-sari stores nationwide, and they account for a large share of all grocery sales. Large companies depend on them to distribute products to remote areas where supermarkets do not exist.
target_summary: Sari-sari stores, small home-based shops, sell goods in tiny quantities and allow credit; over a million exist nationwide.

source: The Olympic Games began in ancient Greece, with the first recorded games held in 776 BCE in Olympia in honor of Zeus. The modern Olympics were revived by Pierre de Coubertin, a French educator, and the first of these took place in Athens in 1896 with 14 nations. The Philippines first competed in 1924 and, for nearly a century, won only silver and bronze medals. That changed in July 2021, when weightlifter Hidilyn Diaz won the country's first Olympic gold in the 55-kilogram class at the Tokyo Games. At the 2024 Paris Olympics, gymnast Carlos Yulo of Manila won gold medals in both the floor exercise and the vault, bringing the Philippines' gold total to three.
target_summary: Hidilyn Diaz won the Philippines' first Olympic gold in 2021.

source: Solar panels convert sunlight directly into electricity using photovoltaic cells, which are usually made of silicon. When light hits the cell, it knocks electrons loose, creating a flow of direct current that an inverter converts into the alternating current used in homes. Most commercial panels today have an efficiency of 15 to 22 percent, meaning that this share of the sunlight reaching the panel becomes electricity. A typical household system of 3 kilowatts can produce roughly 12 kilowatt-hours a day in a sunny country like the Philippines, which is enough to cover much of the electricity needs of an average home. Panels usually come with warranties of 25 years, and rooftop systems can often pay for themselves within five to eight years.
target_summary: Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity at 15 to 22 percent efficiency.

source: Libraries around the world organize books using the Dewey Decimal Classification, a system created by American librarian Melvil Dewey in 1876. It divides all knowledge into ten main classes, each given a range of numbers: for example, 000 is for general works and computer science, 300 for social sciences, 500 for natural sciences and mathematics, and 900 for history and geography. Each class is split into ten divisions, which are then divided again into more specific topics, with decimals added for greater precision. A book on the history of the Philippines, for instance, is placed in the 950s, the number range for Asia. The system makes it possible for readers to find a book quickly, because books on the same subject are shelved next to each other.
target_summary: Melvil Dewey's 1876 system sorts library books into ten subject classes.

source: Arnis, also known as eskrima or kali, is a traditional Filipino martial art that uses sticks, knives, and bare hands for self-defense. Practitioners usually train with two rattan sticks about 28 inches long, learning strikes, blocks, and disarming techniques in flowing patterns. Historians believe that the art developed from the fighting skills used by pre-colonial warriors, and it was practiced in secret during the Spanish period, when weapons were banned, often disguised in folk dances. In 2009, Republic Act 9850 declared arnis the national martial art and sport of the Philippines. It is now taught in public schools and included in the Southeast Asian Games, where Filipino athletes have won many medals.
target_summary: Arnis, a Filipino stick-fighting art, is the national martial art.

source: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, known as Mahatma, led India's nonviolent struggle for independence from British rule. In March 1930, he began the Salt March, walking about 390 kilometers from his ashram near Ahmedabad to the coastal village of Dandi to protest a British tax on salt. Thousands joined him along the way, and when he picked up a lump of natural salt on April 6, it became a powerful act of civil disobedience, leading to the arrest of more than 60,000 people. His philosophy of satyagraha, or truth force, inspired later leaders such as Martin Luther King Jr. India gained independence on August 15, 1947, and Gandhi was assassinated on January 30, 1948.
target_summary: Gandhi led nonviolent protests, and India became independent in 1947.

source: The Magna Carta, or Great Charter, was signed by King John of England on June 15, 1215, at Runnymede, a meadow beside the River Thames. A group of rebellious barons forced the king to accept it after he raised taxes heavily and lost wars in France. The document limited the king's powers and stated that no free man could be imprisoned or punished except by the lawful judgment of his equals. It also promised access to justice and protection of church rights. Pope Innocent III declared the charter invalid within months, and it was reissued several times in revised forms. Although only a few of its clauses remain law in England today, it became a symbol of the rule of law.
target_summary: In 1215, barons forced King John to sign the Magna Carta.

source: The Philippine Statistics Authority reported that the unemployment rate fell to 3.9 percent in April, the lowest level in four years, from 4.7 percent in the same month last year. About 49.3 million Filipinos had jobs, with the most new positions created in wholesale and retail trade, construction, and accommodation services. However, the underemployment rate, which measures workers who want more hours or a second job, remained high at 12.4 percent. Agriculture lost 480,000 jobs as farm workers moved to cities or took jobs abroad. National Economic Development Secretary Marcelo Reyes said the figures show a recovering economy but also stressed the need for training programs to help workers move into higher-paying industries. Youth unemployment was 8.5 percent.
target_summary: Unemployment fell to 3.9 percent in April, a four-year low.

source: Ohm's law describes the relationship between voltage, current, and resistance in an electric circuit. Formulated by German physicist Georg Ohm in 1827, it states that the current flowing through a conductor equals the voltage across it divided by its resistance, written as V equals I times R. Voltage is measured in volts, current in amperes, and resistance in ohms. For example, if a 12-volt battery is connected to a resistor of 4 ohms, a current of 3 amperes will flow. In a series circuit, components share one path and their resistances add up, while in a parallel circuit, the current splits among several branches, so the total resistance becomes smaller.
target_summary: Ohm's law says current equals voltage divided by resistance.

source: The Iligan City government opened a new public market in Barangay Tibanga on June 12, 2025, after eighteen months of construction. The two-story building cost PHP 85 million and houses 240 stalls for vendors selling fish, vegetables, meat, and dry goods. Mayor Rosa Villanueva said the project was funded by a national government loan and city savings. The market includes a rainwater collection system, a waste segregation area, and parking for about 120 motorcycles. Vendors displaced by an earlier fire in 2023 will receive the first fifty stalls at no rent for six months, while the rest will be assigned through a lottery held next week.
target_summary: Iligan opened a PHP 85 million public market in Barangay Tibanga.

source: Juan Luna's painting Spoliarium, which depicts fallen gladiators being dragged out of an arena in ancient Rome, won the first gold medal at the 1884 National Exposition of Fine Arts in Madrid. The enormous canvas measures more than four meters tall and seven meters wide. Luna, who was born in Ilocos Norte in 1857, finished it after months of work in Rome, and many people believe it was a symbol of the suffering of Filipinos under colonial rule. Another Filipino artist, Fernando Amorsolo, became famous for his sunlit paintings of rural life, with farmers planting rice and women washing clothes, and in 1972 he became the first person to be named National Artist for Visual Arts. Spoliarium is displayed in the National Museum in Manila.
target_summary: Juan Luna's huge Spoliarium won gold in Madrid in 1884.

source: A magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck the island of Bohol on October 15, 2013, at 8:12 in the morning, which was a public holiday for the Muslim feast of Eid al-Adha. The epicenter was near the town of Sagbayan, and the quake was caused by a previously unknown fault that scientists later named the North Bohol Fault. It killed 222 people, injured about 800, and damaged more than 73,000 houses and many historic churches, including the Loboc Church and the Baclayon Church, which dated back to the Spanish period. Roads and bridges were broken, and about 370,000 people were forced to leave their homes. International and local groups helped to rebuild, and many of the damaged churches were restored over the following years.
target_summary: A magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck Bohol on October 15, 2013.

source: The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 6.5 percent on Thursday, saying that inflation has eased to 3.9 percent in May from 4.4 percent in April. Governor Eli Santiago said the decision reflects the need to balance price stability with economic growth, which slowed to 5.3 percent in the first quarter. Economists polled by a news agency had expected the central bank to hold rates. However, analysts warned that oil prices and a weaker peso, which closed at PHP 57.8 against the dollar, could push inflation up again later this year. The next policy meeting is scheduled for August 14.
target_summary: The central bank held its interest rate at 6.5 percent.

source: In March 1521, the Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan, sailing for Spain, reached the islands that would later be called the Philippines. He made an alliance with Rajah Humabon of Cebu, and many of the islanders were baptized as Christians. Magellan then agreed to help Humabon fight a rival chief, Lapulapu, who ruled the island of Mactan and refused to submit to Spanish authority. On April 27, 1521, Magellan landed with about 50 armed men, but they were outnumbered by hundreds of Lapulapu's warriors. Magellan was killed in the battle. Lapulapu is therefore remembered as the first Filipino to resist foreign colonization, and a statue of him stands in Mactan.
target_summary: Lapulapu's warriors killed Magellan at Mactan on April 27, 1521.

source: The RMS Titanic, a British passenger liner and the largest ship in the world at the time, sank in the North Atlantic on April 15, 1912, during its first voyage from Southampton to New York. Four days after leaving England, at 11:40 p.m. on April 14, it struck an iceberg, which tore open several of its watertight compartments. The ship sank in about two hours and forty minutes. Of the roughly 2,224 people on board, more than 1,500 died, partly because there were lifeboats for only about half of the passengers. The liner Carpathia rescued about 710 survivors. The disaster led to new international safety rules, including a requirement for enough lifeboats for everyone and constant radio watch.
target_summary: The Titanic hit an iceberg and sank in April 1912.

source: Sleep is essential for physical health and mental performance. Most adults need seven to nine hours each night, while teenagers need about eight to ten. During sleep, the brain cycles through several stages roughly every 90 minutes, including light sleep, deep sleep, and rapid eye movement sleep, which is when most vivid dreams occur. Deep sleep helps the body repair tissues and strengthen the immune system, while REM sleep supports memory and learning. The brain releases a hormone called melatonin when it gets dark, signaling that it is time to rest. Regular lack of sleep has been linked to weight gain, poor concentration, heart disease, and a higher risk of accidents.
target_summary: Adults need seven to nine hours of sleep each night.

source: The Philippine government is divided into three branches, a principle known as separation of powers. The executive branch, headed by the President, carries out the laws; the President serves a single term of six years and cannot be reelected. The legislative branch, called Congress, makes laws and is divided into the Senate, which has 24 members elected nationwide, and the House of Representatives, whose members represent districts and party-list groups. The judicial branch, led by the Supreme Court with 15 justices, interprets the laws and decides whether they follow the Constitution. This system of checks and balances is meant to keep any one branch from becoming too powerful, as the 1987 Constitution was written after the Marcos dictatorship.
target_summary: The Philippines divides power among executive, legislative, and judicial branches.

source: The Moon's appearance changes over a cycle of about 29.5 days, known as the lunar cycle, as the Moon orbits Earth and different parts of its sunlit half become visible. The cycle starts with the new moon, when the side facing us is dark and the Moon is almost invisible. As it moves, the lit part grows through the waxing crescent, the first quarter, and the waxing gibbous phases until the full moon, when the entire face is lit. Afterward, the lit part shrinks through the waning gibbous, the last quarter, and the waning crescent phases. The Moon does not make its own light but reflects sunlight. Many Filipino farmers and fishermen have traditionally used the lunar cycle to decide when to plant or fish.
target_summary: The Moon's phases repeat every 29.5 days as it reflects sunlight.

source: An ancestral house in Silay City, Negros Occidental, has reopened as a museum after a three-year restoration costing PHP 32 million. Built in 1927 by a sugar planter, the two-story house features a wooden ceiling painted with flowers, a grand staircase, and floors of narra and molave wood. Conservation architect Daniel Fortuna said that termites had destroyed nearly one fifth of the structure, and that craftsmen had to replace the damaged beams using old photographs as a guide. The museum displays furniture, family portraits, and farming tools, and it also hosts concerts every first Friday of the month. Entrance is PHP 100 for adults, while students and senior citizens pay half. Officials expect 30,000 visitors in the first year.
target_summary: A restored 1927 house in Silay reopened as a museum.

source: Jose Rizal, the national hero of the Philippines, was born on June 19, 1861, in Calamba, Laguna. He studied medicine in Manila and Madrid and became a skilled eye doctor, writer, painter, and linguist who spoke more than ten languages. His two novels, Noli Me Tangere, published in 1887, and El Filibusterismo, published in 1891, exposed the abuses of Spanish colonial rule and the Catholic friars. Rizal believed in peaceful reform rather than armed revolt. Colonial authorities arrested him in 1896 and accused him of sedition and rebellion. After a military trial, he was executed by firing squad at Bagumbayan, now Rizal Park, on December 30, 1896, at the age of 35.
target_summary: Jose Rizal, born in 1861, wrote two novels against Spanish rule.

source: The Philippines is highly exposed to natural hazards because of its location. It lies along the Pacific Ring of Fire and the typhoon belt, and it is also threatened by flooding, landslides, and sea level rise. The 2022 World Risk Report ranked it as the country with the highest disaster risk in the world, combining the likelihood of extreme events with the vulnerability of its people. To respond, Republic Act 10121, passed in 2010, created the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council and required local governments to set aside at least five percent of their budget for disaster preparedness. Many communities now practice earthquake drills, build evacuation centers, and use early warning systems for floods and storm surges.
target_summary: The Philippines ranked first in the 2022 World Risk Report.

source: Water service in six barangays of Marawi City will be interrupted for 36 hours starting Saturday night because of repairs to the main pipeline in Barangay Datu Saber. The Marawi Water District said that workers will replace a 400-meter section of corroded pipe that has caused frequent leaks and low water pressure since 2022. About 5,200 households will be affected. Water tankers will visit each barangay twice a day to supply residents, and refilling stations will remain open until midnight. The district apologized for the inconvenience and promised that service will return by Monday afternoon. Residents were advised to store enough water for drinking, cooking, and sanitation.
target_summary: Six Marawi barangays lose water for 36 hours during repairs.

source: A group of marine biologists from Mindanao State University recorded 14 whale sharks feeding off the coast of Sarangani Bay during a three-day survey in March. The researchers attached small tags to five of the animals to track their movement and found that they traveled as far as 90 kilometers north in less than a week. Whale sharks, the largest fish in the world, can grow up to 12 meters and live for 70 years, but they are listed as endangered. The team said fishing nets and boat strikes remain the main dangers. They have asked local governments to create a protected zone and limit boat speeds near feeding areas.
target_summary: Mindanao State University researchers recorded 14 whale sharks in Sarangani Bay.

source: Earth has seasons because its axis is tilted by about 23.5 degrees relative to its orbit around the Sun. When the Northern Hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun, it receives more direct sunlight and longer days, which causes summer, while the Southern Hemisphere experiences winter. Six months later, the situation is reversed. The solstices, around June 21 and December 21, mark the longest and shortest days of the year, and during the equinoxes, in March and September, day and night are nearly equal in length. The distance from the Sun does not cause the seasons; in fact, Earth is closest to the Sun in early January. Countries near the equator, such as the Philippines, have little change in day length and instead have wet and dry seasons.
target_summary: Earth's 23.5-degree axial tilt causes seasons, not distance from the Sun.

source: Authorities in Agusan del Norte have started a program to plant 1.5 million trees in a single day, hoping to restore forests that have been lost to farming and charcoal making. Schoolchildren, soldiers, and local volunteers fanned out across 10 municipalities, and the governor planted the first seedling at a ceremony in Butuan City. The province's goal is to increase forest cover from 12 percent to 30 percent of its land by 2032. Environmental groups welcomed the effort but warned that many seedlings die if they are not watered during the dry season, and that protecting existing forests is cheaper than replanting. A tree-tracking app allows participants to record the location of their trees and receive follow-up reminders.
target_summary: Agusan del Norte will plant 1.5 million trees in one day.

source: Matter commonly exists in three states: solid, liquid, and gas, depending on how tightly its particles are packed and how fast they move. In a solid, the particles are locked in place and only vibrate, so the substance keeps its shape. In a liquid, the particles are close but can slide past each other, so a liquid takes the shape of its container but has a fixed volume. In a gas, the particles are far apart and move freely, so a gas fills any space available. Changing the temperature can change the state. At normal sea level pressure, water freezes into ice at 0 degrees Celsius and boils into steam at 100 degrees Celsius. A fourth state, plasma, occurs at extremely high temperatures and is found in lightning and the Sun.
target_summary: Matter exists as solid, liquid, or gas depending on particle spacing.

source: The internet is a global network of computers that communicate by sending small chunks of data called packets. Every device is identified by an Internet Protocol address, and the Domain Name System acts like a phone book, translating names such as example.com into numerical addresses. When someone opens a web page, the request travels through routers owned by internet service providers until it reaches a server, which sends the requested data back in packets that are reassembled in the correct order by the TCP protocol. The earliest ancestor of the internet, ARPANET, sent its first message between two American universities in October 1969. The message was supposed to read LOGIN, but the system crashed after the first two letters.
target_summary: The internet sends data as packets between devices using IP addresses.

source: The Great Wall of China is not a single wall but a series of fortifications built by different dynasties over more than two thousand years to protect the northern borders from invading nomads. Around 221 BCE, Emperor Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor of unified China, ordered earlier walls to be connected. Most of the wall that tourists visit today, however, was built during the Ming dynasty between the fourteenth and seventeenth centuries using bricks and stone. All of its branches together measure more than 21,000 kilometers. Contrary to a popular myth, the wall cannot be seen from the Moon with the naked eye, since it is long but very narrow.
target_summary: The Great Wall is a chain of fortifications over 21,000 kilometers.

source: The Chocolate Hills in Bohol are a group of more than 1,200 cone-shaped hills spread over an area of about 50 square kilometers in the towns of Carmen, Batuan, and Sagbayan. The hills measure between 30 and 120 meters in height and are covered with grass that turns chocolate brown during the dry season, giving them their name. Geologists believe that they were formed from the uplift of ancient coral deposits and later shaped by rainfall and erosion, although Filipino folklore tells of two giants who threw rocks at each other until they became friends and left behind the rocks. The hills were declared a National Geological Monument in 1988, and visitors can climb 214 steps to a viewing deck in Carmen.
target_summary: Bohol's Chocolate Hills are over 1,200 cone-shaped hills that turn brown.

source: The greenhouse effect is a natural process in which certain gases in the atmosphere, such as carbon dioxide, methane, and water vapor, trap some of the heat radiated from Earth's surface, keeping the planet warm enough for life. Without it, the average temperature would be about minus 18 degrees Celsius instead of the present 15 degrees. However, burning coal, oil, and gas has raised the carbon dioxide concentration from about 280 parts per million before the Industrial Revolution to more than 420 today. As a result, global average temperatures have risen by about 1.1 degrees Celsius since the late 1800s, causing glaciers to melt, sea levels to rise, and extreme weather to become more frequent.
target_summary: Greenhouse gases trap heat, and burning fossil fuels has intensified warming.

source: Basketball was invented in December 1891 by James Naismith, a Canadian physical education teacher at a school in Springfield, Massachusetts. Looking for an indoor game to keep students active during the cold winter, he nailed two peach baskets to the walls of the gym, ten feet above the floor, and wrote 13 basic rules. Players could not run while holding the ball, and after each score someone had to climb a ladder to retrieve it. The sport spread quickly through schools and YMCA clubs, and it became an Olympic event in 1936. The sport arrived in the Philippines through the American colonial period, and in 1975 the country founded the Philippine Basketball Association, the first professional basketball league in Asia.
target_summary: James Naismith invented basketball in 1891 using peach baskets and 13 rules.

source: On June 12, 1898, General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed the independence of the Philippines from the balcony of his house in Kawit, Cavite. The Act of the Declaration of Independence was read aloud before a crowd, and the Philippine flag, sewn in Hong Kong by Marcela Agoncillo with her daughter and Delfina Herbosa de Natividad, was raised for the first time in the country. A band also played the national march composed by Julian Felipe, which later became the national anthem. However, the declaration was not recognized by Spain or the United States, which took control of the islands after the Treaty of Paris in December 1898. Independence Day is celebrated every June 12.
target_summary: Aguinaldo declared Philippine independence at Kawit on June 12, 1898.

source: The World Health Organization recommends that adults aged 18 to 64 do at least 150 to 300 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity, such as brisk walking or cycling, every week. Alternatively, 75 to 150 minutes of vigorous activity like running or swimming laps will give similar benefits. Adults should also do muscle-strengthening exercises involving all major muscle groups on at least two days a week. Regular exercise lowers the risk of heart disease, type 2 diabetes, and some cancers, and it improves sleep and mood. People who are not used to exercising should start with short sessions of ten minutes and gradually increase the time to avoid injuries.
target_summary: The WHO advises adults 150 to 300 weekly exercise minutes.

source: The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration, known as PAGASA, gives local names to tropical cyclones that enter or form inside the Philippine Area of Responsibility. The names come from four sets of 25 names, arranged alphabetically, and each set is reused every four years. Names are chosen to be short and easy to remember, such as Ambo, Bising, and Carina. When a storm causes more than 1 billion pesos in damage or kills at least 300 people, its name is retired and replaced, as happened with Yolanda in 2013 and Ondoy in 2009. In addition to the name, PAGASA uses a five-level Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal system, from one to five, to warn the public about expected wind strength and the time before the storm arrives.
target_summary: PAGASA names storms from four rotating sets of 25 names.

source: Around 1440, a German goldsmith named Johannes Gutenberg developed a printing press in the city of Mainz that used movable metal type. Before this invention, books were copied by hand, a slow process that made them rare and expensive. Gutenberg combined a screw press similar to those used for wine, oil-based ink, and individual metal letters that could be rearranged and reused. His most famous work, the Gutenberg Bible, was printed around 1455, with about 180 copies. Within 50 years, printing presses operated in more than 250 European cities and had produced millions of books, spreading literacy, scientific ideas, and religious debate, which helped drive the Renaissance and the Reformation.
target_summary: Gutenberg developed the movable-type printing press in Mainz around 1440.

source: Del Monte Philippines operates one of the largest pineapple plantations in the world in Bukidnon, in the highlands of Mindanao. The company began there in 1926 at the site of a former military camp, taking advantage of the volcanic soil, cool temperatures, and ample rainfall. Today, its fields stretch across thousands of hectares and employ many local residents, and the pineapples are canned or made into juice and exported to dozens of countries. The Philippines is one of the top producers of pineapple globally. While the plantations bring jobs and income, critics have raised concerns about the pesticide use, the displacement of indigenous communities from ancestral land, and the low wages paid to contract workers during the harvest.
target_summary: Del Monte began its Bukidnon highland pineapple plantation in 1926.

source: Remittances from Filipinos working abroad are one of the pillars of the Philippine economy. In recent years, overseas Filipino workers have sent home more than 35 billion US dollars annually, which is equal to roughly nine percent of the country's gross domestic product. The money comes mainly from the United States, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, and Japan, and it is spent mostly on food, housing, education, and health care for the family members left behind. Economists say remittances help keep consumer spending strong and the peso stable, although they also create dependence on foreign labor markets. Millions of Filipinos work abroad as nurses, seafarers, domestic helpers, and engineers, and many families spend years separated from each other.
target_summary: Overseas Filipinos send over 35 billion dollars home each year.

source: Coffee farmers in Sultan Kudarat expect their best harvest in a decade after rains arrived at the right time during flowering. The Department of Agriculture estimates that the province will produce 3,100 metric tons of green coffee beans this season, about 40 percent more than last year. Most of the crop is robusta, but a growing number of farmers have planted arabica on the cooler slopes of the Daguma range. Prices have also improved, with farm-gate prices for robusta at PHP 150 per kilo, compared to PHP 110 last year. A farmers' cooperative in Bagumbayan said it signed a contract to deliver 200 tons to a roaster in Manila. Many farmers plan to use the extra income to repair their drying sheds.
target_summary: Sultan Kudarat expects 3,100 tons of coffee, 40 percent more.

source: The city of Haverdam in the Netherlands has begun building a rooftop forest on top of a large shopping center. When finished, the green space will cover 5,000 square meters and include 2,000 plants, including 120 trees. The project aims to reduce the heat in the city center, absorb rainwater, and provide a habitat for birds and insects. City planners said that the roof is built to carry the weight of soil that is 60 centimeters deep. The project costs 4 million euros, half of which is paid by the city and half by the mall owner. Haverdam already has more than 360,000 square meters of green roofs, and the city plans to reach one million by 2035.
target_summary: Haverdam is building a rooftop forest on a shopping center.

source: Mayon Volcano in Albay province is famous for its almost perfect cone shape and stands about 2,462 meters above sea level. It is the most active volcano in the Philippines and has erupted more than 50 times in recorded history, with the most destructive eruption occurring in 1814, which buried the town of Cagsawa and killed more than 1,200 people. Today, the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology monitors it with seismographs and gas sensors, and a permanent danger zone of six kilometers around the crater is closed to residents. During eruptions, thousands of families in nearby towns move to evacuation centers until the alert level is lowered.
target_summary: Mayon, 2,462 meters high, is the Philippines' most active volcano.

source: Authorities in Cotabato City arrested four suspects on Monday for running an illegal online gambling operation inside a rented warehouse. Police seized 65 computers, 40 mobile phones, and PHP 1.2 million in cash during the raid, which began at 9 a.m. after two weeks of surveillance. The group allegedly accepted bets on basketball and cockfighting through a website and hired about 30 agents. Police said that the suspects face charges under the Anti-Illegal Gambling Law and could be jailed for up to six years. The warehouse owner, who claimed he was not aware of the activities, will be questioned by investigators this week.
target_summary: Cotabato police raided a warehouse and arrested four gambling suspects.

source: Weather forecasters warned on Wednesday that a La Nina episode is likely to develop between October and December, bringing above-normal rainfall to many parts of the country. The state weather bureau estimated a 70 percent chance that sea temperatures in the central Pacific will fall below average, which usually leads to more tropical cyclones and heavier rain in the Philippines. Mindanao and the Visayas are expected to receive the largest increase in rain, raising the risk of floods and landslides. Farmers were advised to adjust their planting calendars, clear drainage canals, and store harvested crops in dry places. The Department of Education said it was prepared to move classes online in areas hit by flooding. The weather bureau will issue a new update every two weeks.
target_summary: Forecasters see a 70 percent chance of La Nina this year.

source: The 2020 Census of Population and Housing counted about 109 million Filipinos, making the Philippines the thirteenth most populous country in the world. The population grew at an average of 1.63 percent each year between 2015 and 2020, which is slower than in previous decades. The median age is about 25, which means that half the population is younger than that, a feature economists call a demographic dividend because it offers a large working-age population. About half the people live in urban areas, and Metro Manila alone is home to roughly 13 million residents. source: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation, or CPR, is a lifesaving technique used when someone's heart stops beating. If a person collapses and does not respond or breathe normally, first call emergency services and ask someone to bring a defibrillator if one is available. Then place the heel of one hand on the center of the chest, put the other hand on top, and push hard and fast, at least five centimeters deep, at a rate of 100 to 120 compressions per minute, which matches the beat of the song Stayin' Alive. Trained rescuers give two rescue breaths after every 30 compressions. Continue until medical help arrives or the person starts breathing. Bystanders who are not trained can use compressions only, which still doubles the chance of survival.
target_summary: For a collapsed person, call for help and start chest compressions.

source: The Great Pyramid of Giza, built around 2560 BCE as the tomb of the Egyptian pharaoh Khufu, is the oldest and largest of the three pyramids on the Giza plateau near modern Cairo. It originally stood about 146.6 meters tall, and it remained the tallest human-made structure in the world for nearly 3,800 years. The pyramid contains an estimated 2.3 million blocks of limestone and granite, some weighing several tons, which were cut, transported, and stacked by thousands of skilled workers rather than slaves, according to archaeological evidence. Inside are three main chambers connected by narrow passages. It is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World that still exists today.
target_summary: The Great Pyramid of Giza was built for Pharaoh Khufu.

source: The Mindanao Development Authority and a group of local businesses launched a campaign this week to promote Mindanao as a major source of coconut-based products. Organizers expect orders worth PHP 800 million from buyers in Japan, South Korea, and Europe. source: The Maranao people live around Lake Lanao in Mindanao, and their name means people of the lake. Their homeland includes Marawi City and parts of Lanao del Sur and Lanao del Norte. Most Maranao are Muslim, and their culture has produced a rich tradition of art. The torogan, a large ancestral house raised on tall wooden posts, was traditionally the home of a sultan or datu, and its beams are carved with okir, a flowing design of vines and leaves. Maranao craftsmen also create brass betel boxes, woven malongs, and the kulintang, a set of eight small gongs played together in an ensemble. The Maranao epic Darangen, which tells of ancient heroes, was named a UNESCO Masterpiece of Intangible Heritage in 2005.
target_summary: The Maranao of Lake Lanao are known for okir and kulintang.

source: Gross domestic product, or GDP, is the total value of all final goods and services produced inside a country in a given period, usually a year or a quarter. Economists use it to measure the size of an economy and how fast it is growing. The concept was developed in the 1930s by economist Simon Kuznets for the United States Congress. GDP can be calculated by adding consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports. Critics point out that it does not capture unpaid work such as housework, the quality of the environment, or how evenly income is shared. For this reason, researchers often look at other measures as well, such as the Human Development Index, which includes health and education.
target_summary: GDP totals the final goods and services a country produces yearly.

source: Phishing is a trick in which criminals send emails, text messages, or social media posts that pretend to come from trusted organizations, such as banks or delivery companies, to steal passwords and financial information. These messages often create a sense of urgency, claiming that an account will be closed or that a payment is overdue. They usually contain a link to a fake website that looks identical to the real one. Warning signs include spelling mistakes, a sender address that does not match the company, and unexpected attachments. To stay safe, never click suspicious links, type the website address yourself, and call the company using the number on your card. Report phishing messages to your bank and delete them.
target_summary: Phishing messages imitate trusted organizations to steal passwords and information.

source: The water cycle describes how water moves between the oceans, the air, and the land. Heat from the sun causes water to evaporate from oceans, lakes, and rivers, while plants release additional vapor through their leaves in a process called transpiration. As the vapor rises, it cools and condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds. When the droplets grow heavy enough, they fall as rain, snow, sleet, or hail. Some of this water flows over the ground into streams and rivers, and some soaks into the soil and becomes groundwater. About 97 percent of Earth's water is salty ocean water, and less than one percent is easily available freshwater.
target_summary: The water cycle moves water between oceans, air, and land.

source: Most websites are built using three core technologies that work together in the browser. HyperText Markup Language, or HTML, defines the structure and content of a page, such as headings, paragraphs, images, and links. Cascading Style Sheets, or CSS, controls how that content looks, including colors, fonts, spacing, and layout, and it allows the same page to adapt to phones and large monitors. JavaScript adds interactivity, for example responding to button clicks, validating forms, and loading new data without refreshing the page. Behind the scenes, a server running languages such as Python, PHP, or JavaScript on Node.js processes requests and communicates with a database. Developers use browser tools to inspect and debug pages, and frameworks like React help them organize large projects.
target_summary: HTML structures pages, CSS styles them, and JavaScript adds interactivity.

source: The Philippines adopted the K to 12 basic education program through Republic Act 10533, signed in 2013, which added two years to the previous ten-year system. Under the program, students complete one year of kindergarten, six years of elementary school, four years of junior high school, and two years of senior high school, where they choose a track such as academic, technical-vocational, or sports and arts. Supporters said the extra years would prepare graduates for jobs and align the country with international standards, since the Philippines was one of the last countries with only ten years of basic education. Critics pointed to a shortage of classrooms and teachers, and to the extra expense that fell on poor families.
target_summary: Republic Act 10533 added two years through K to 12.

source: An earthquake happens when stored energy in the crust is suddenly released along a fault, sending seismic waves through the ground. The point underground where the rupture begins is the focus, and the spot directly above it on the surface is the epicenter. Scientists measure the energy released using the moment magnitude scale, where each whole number increase means about 32 times more energy. A magnitude 7 earthquake therefore releases roughly 32 times the energy of a magnitude 6. Seismographs record the waves, and primary waves, which arrive first, are followed by slower but more destructive secondary and surface waves. The most powerful earthquake ever recorded was a magnitude 9.5 in Chile in 1960.
target_summary: Earthquakes release stored energy along faults as seismic waves.

source: Experts recommend the drop, cover, and hold on procedure during an earthquake. As soon as shaking starts, drop to your hands and knees so that you do not fall, cover your head and neck with your arms, and crawl under a sturdy desk or table if there is one nearby. Then hold on to it until the shaking stops. Do not run outside, since falling glass and debris are the biggest danger near buildings, and do not stand in doorways, which are not stronger than the rest of the house. After the shaking stops, check yourself and others for injuries, expect aftershocks, and move to open ground if the building is damaged. The Philippines holds nationwide earthquake drills four times a year to help citizens practice.
target_summary: In an earthquake, drop, cover your head and neck, and hold on.

Airport officials said ground crew discovered feathers and a small dent on the engine cowling during a routine inspection at 6:40 a.m. All 168 passengers were given meal vouchers, and 12 travelers with connecting flights were rebooked at no cost. The plane was replaced with another aircraft that departed at 11:55 a.m. and arrived in Cagayan de Oro just after one in the afternoon. No one was hurt, and the airline said the damaged engine will undergo full maintenance checks.

source: Earth's outer shell is broken into large slabs of rock called tectonic plates, which slowly move on top of a hotter, softer layer of the mantle at a speed of a few centimeters per year, about as fast as fingernails grow. Where plates collide, one may slide under the other, forming deep ocean trenches and volcanic mountain chains. Where they pull apart, new crust is created, as in the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. The Pacific Ring of Fire, a horseshoe-shaped zone stretching about 40,000 kilometers around the Pacific Ocean, contains roughly 75 percent of the world's active volcanoes and produces about 90 percent of its earthquakes. source: Earth's outer shell is broken into large slabs of rock called tectonic plates, which slowly move on top of a hotter, softer layer of the mantle at a speed of a few centimeters per year, about as fast as fingernails grow. Where plates collide, one may slide under the other, forming deep ocean trenches and volcanic mountain chains. Where they pull apart, new crust is created, as in the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. The Pacific Ring of Fire, a horseshoe-shaped zone stretching about 40,000 kilometers around the Pacific Ocean, contains roughly 75 percent of the world's active volcanoes and produces about 90 percent of its earthquakes. source: Computers store all information using the binary system, which has only two digits, zero and one, because electronic circuits can easily represent two states, on and off. Each binary digit is called a bit, and eight bits make up one byte, which can represent 256 different values, enough for a single letter or symbol in the ASCII character set. To convert a binary number to decimal, each digit is multiplied by a power of two, starting from the right. For example, the binary number 1101 equals 8 plus 4 plus 0 plus 1, which is 13 in decimal. Larger units include the kilobyte, megabyte, and gigabyte, which are roughly a thousand, a million, and a billion bytes. Photos, music, and videos are all stored as long sequences of bits.
target_summary: Computers store data in binary; eight bits make one byte.

source: The Panagbenga Festival, also known as the Baguio Flower Festival, is held every February in Baguio City to celebrate the blooming of flowers. The name comes from a Kankanaey word meaning a season of blossoming. The festival began in the mid-1990s as a way to help the city recover from the devastating earthquake of July 1990, which killed more than 1,600 people in Luzon and badly damaged Baguio. Its highlights include a parade of floats decorated with thousands of fresh flowers and street dancing performed in costumes inspired by flowers and by the Cordillera region. Lasting about a month, the festival draws hundreds of thousands of visitors and is one of the most important events for the local economy.
target_summary: Baguio's Panagbenga flower festival began after the 1990 earthquake.

source: Adobo is often called the unofficial national dish of the Philippines. It is made by simmering chicken, pork, or both in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, black peppercorns, and bay leaves until the meat is tender and the sauce thickens. Historians believe that cooking meat in vinegar and salt was a method of preservation used by Filipinos long before the Spaniards arrived, which was necessary in the hot, humid climate. The Spanish colonizers later gave the dish its name, derived from the word adobar, which means to marinate. Each region and family has its own version: some add coconut milk, as in the Bicol area, while others use turmeric or leave out soy sauce completely.
target_summary: Adobo is a Philippine dish of meat simmered in vinegar.

source: Tricycle drivers in Pagadian City won a fare increase on Tuesday after three weeks of talks with the city council. Drivers had asked for a larger increase because gasoline now costs PHP 66 a liter and they must also pay PHP 600 a month for their franchise fee. Student, senior citizen, and disabled passengers will continue to receive a 20 percent discount. The council also ordered all tricycles to display a printed fare chart, and passengers can file complaints at a hotline.

source: Manny Pacquiao, born on December 17, 1978, in Kibawe, Bukidnon, grew up in extreme poverty in General Santos City and began boxing as a teenager to help feed his family. source: Camiguin is a pear-shaped island province in northern Mindanao, often called the Island Born of Fire because it has seven volcanoes, though only Mount Hibok-Hibok is classified as active. The island is just about 29 kilometers long and 14 kilometers wide, and yet it offers waterfalls, hot springs, and white-sand beaches. One of its most remarkable sites is the Sunken Cemetery, which was submerged after the eruption of Vulcan Daan in 1871, and is now marked by a large cross, and divers and snorkelers can see the old headstones underwater. Every October, Camiguin celebrates the Lanzones Festival, honoring the sweet fruit that grows abundantly there. Because of strict rules on construction, the island has few large resorts and remains peaceful.
target_summary: Camiguin, the Island Born of Fire, has seven volcanoes in Mindanao.

source: A team of five high school students from Davao City won the national robotics championship in Quezon City on Sunday with a machine that sorts plastic bottles by color. Their robot, named Ayos, uses a camera and a small computer to identify the bottles, then pushes them into the correct bin with a robotic arm made of recycled parts. In the final round, it correctly sorted 47 of 50 bottles in under three minutes, beating 31 teams from across the country. Team coach Mr. Joel Velasco said that the students built the robot over four months, meeting after classes and on weekends, with a budget of only PHP 25,000. The winners will represent the Philippines at an international contest in Singapore in December.

source: Rocks are divided into three main types according to how they form. Igneous rocks, such as granite and basalt, form when molten rock, called magma or lava, cools and hardens, either underground or after a volcanic eruption. Sedimentary rocks, such as sandstone, limestone, and shale, form when pieces of other rocks, shells, and plant remains settle in layers and are pressed together over millions of years; fossils are usually found in them. Metamorphic rocks, such as marble and slate, are created when existing rocks are changed by intense heat and pressure deep inside the Earth without melting. The rock cycle describes how any of these types can turn into another. The Philippines has many igneous rocks because of its numerous volcanoes, and Bohol's Chocolate Hills are made of limestone.
target_summary: Rocks are igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic, depending on how they form.

source: The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world. An adult can stand about one meter tall and has a wingspan of up to two meters, with a shaggy crest of feathers around its head that gives it a distinctive look. It feeds on monkeys, flying lemurs, snakes, and large birds, which is why it is also called the monkey-eating eagle. The bird lives only in a few forests of Luzon, Samar, Leyte, and Mindanao, and the largest population lives in Mindanao. It is critically endangered, with only a few hundred pairs left in the wild, because of logging and hunting. The Philippine Eagle Center in Davao City has bred and released several eagles.
target_summary: The Philippine eagle is a huge, critically endangered national bird.

source: Deoxyribonucleic acid, or DNA, is the molecule that carries the genetic instructions for living things. Its structure, a twisted ladder known as the double helix, was described in 1953 by James Watson and Francis Crick, who built on X-ray images taken by Rosalind Franklin. The rungs of the ladder are made of pairs of four chemical bases: adenine pairs with thymine, and cytosine pairs with guanine. The human genome contains about three billion base pairs and roughly 20,000 genes, packaged into 23 pairs of chromosomes inside almost every cell. Any two people share about 99.9 percent of their DNA, so tiny differences explain our individual traits.
target_summary: DNA carries genetic instructions in a double helix structure.

Two of its hearts pump blood through the gills, while the third circulates it to the rest of the body. Octopuses can change both color and skin texture within a fraction of a second by controlling thousands of cells called chromatophores, helping them hide from predators. Most species live only one to five years, and females usually die soon after their eggs hatch.

source: The International Space Station is a large laboratory that orbits Earth at an altitude of about 400 kilometers. It travels at a speed of around 28,000 kilometers per hour, circling the planet once every 90 minutes, which means the astronauts on board see about 16 sunrises and sunsets every day. The first piece was launched in 1998, and people have lived on board continuously since November 2000. The station is a joint project of the United States, Russia, Europe, Japan, and Canada, and it is about the size of a football field. Astronauts conduct experiments on how the human body and materials behave in microgravity, and they typically stay for about six months before returning to Earth in a capsule.
target_summary: The International Space Station orbits 400 kilometers up every 90 minutes.

source: The National Telecommunications Commission said that mobile networks blocked more than 1.2 million spam and scam text messages in a single week, after it ordered all carriers to filter suspicious links. Most of the blocked messages claimed that recipients had won a prize or needed to update their e-wallet accounts, and many included links to fake websites that steal passwords. The commission also deactivated 38,000 SIM cards that were registered with false identities. Officials reminded the public that banks and e-wallet companies never ask customers to share one-time passwords or click links in text messages. Victims were advised to report scams through a hotline and keep screenshots as evidence. Cybercrime cases rose by 21 percent last year.
target_summary: Mobile networks blocked over 1.2 million scam texts in one week.

source: A measles vaccination drive in the province of Sulu has reached 91 percent of children under five, surpassing the national target of 90 percent, the provincial health office reported. Health workers visited homes, mosques, and schools over four weeks and vaccinated 38,500 children, using boats to reach 14 island barangays. The campaign followed an outbreak last year that sickened 640 children and killed nine. Provincial health officer Dr. Nasser Jaafar said that misinformation and distrust had been the biggest obstacles, and that religious leaders helped by assuring parents that the vaccine was safe. Children who missed the drive can still get free shots at their local health centers every Wednesday until the end of the month.
target_summary: Sulu vaccinated 38,500 children against measles, reaching 91 percent.

source: Pupils at San Isidro Elementary School in Bukidnon have been receiving free hot breakfast every morning since January under a feeding program funded by the municipal government and a local rice mill. About 420 children from kindergarten to grade six get a bowl of rice porridge with egg and vegetables, prepared by a rotating group of 25 parent volunteers. Teachers report that attendance rose from 82 percent to 94 percent in three months, and the number of underweight children dropped from 96 to 61. Principal Lorna Bacalso said that pupils now concentrate better in morning classes. The program costs about PHP 18 per child a day, and the municipality hopes to extend it to five more schools next year.
target_summary: Free breakfast at San Isidro Elementary raised attendance to 94 percent.

source: The University of the Philippines Mindanao will offer a new four-year degree in data science starting in the next academic year, the first of its kind in the region. Students will study programming, statistics, machine learning, and database management, and they will complete a six-month internship with partner companies. The program will admit 40 students in its first batch, and applicants must have at least a grade of 85 in mathematics. Tuition will follow the university's standard rate of PHP 1,000 per unit for non-scholars. Dean Maria Teodoro said that demand for data analysts in Mindanao has grown by 25 percent annually, but few local graduates have the necessary skills.
target_summary: UP Mindanao will launch the region's first data science degree.

source: The Katipunan, a secret revolutionary society, was founded by Andres Bonifacio and other patriots in Manila on July 7, 1892, the same night that Jose Rizal was exiled to Dapitan. Bonifacio, a warehouse worker from a poor family in Tondo, wanted to free the Philippines from Spanish rule by force. Members took a blood oath, used code names, and spread across Luzon and the Visayas, eventually reaching tens of thousands. The society was discovered by Spanish authorities in August 1896, which led Bonifacio and his followers to tear up their community tax certificates in what is known as the Cry of Pugad Lawin and begin the Philippine Revolution.
target_summary: Andres Bonifacio founded the secret Katipunan on July 7, 1892.

source: A relational database stores information in tables made of rows and columns, similar to spreadsheets, and links the tables together through shared values. The relational model was proposed in 1970 by Edgar F. Codd, a researcher at IBM, and it remains the basis for popular systems such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, and Oracle. Each table has a primary key, a column that uniquely identifies every row, while a foreign key in another table refers to it to create a relationship. Developers use Structured Query Language, or SQL, to create, read, update, and delete data. Good design avoids duplicate information by splitting data into separate tables, a process known as normalization, which keeps records consistent and easier to update.
target_summary: Relational databases store data in linked tables queried with SQL.

source: Teachers in Misamis Oriental began a three-day strike on Monday to demand overdue allowances and smaller class sizes. The Alliance of Concerned Teachers said that 1,200 educators have not received their PHP 5,000 annual teaching allowance for the current school year. Many public school classrooms hold up to 55 students, well above the recommended limit of 35. The Department of Education regional director called the strike unauthorized but promised to release the allowances by the end of the month. Parents were advised to keep their children at home, as only skeleton classes would run in 18 elementary schools during the walkout.

source: The EDSA People Power Revolution took place from February 22 to 25, 1986, along Epifanio de los Santos Avenue in Metro Manila. It began after a disputed snap presidential election in which Ferdinand Marcos, who had ruled for more than 20 years, was declared the winner over Corazon Aquino, the widow of assassinated senator Benigno Aquino Jr. Defense Minister Juan Ponce Enrile and General Fidel Ramos broke away from the government, and Cardinal Jaime Sin urged citizens to protect them. Up to two million Filipinos gathered peacefully, offering flowers and prayers to soldiers and tanks. On February 25, Marcos and his family fled to Hawaii, and Aquino was sworn in as president.
target_summary: A peaceful 1986 uprising on EDSA forced Marcos to flee.

source: Mount Pinatubo, a volcano about 90 kilometers northwest of Manila, erupted on June 15, 1991, in the second-largest volcanic eruption of the twentieth century. After centuries of silence, the volcano gave warning signs in the preceding months, and scientists from the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology and the United States Geological Survey advised an evacuation of tens of thousands of people, which saved many lives. The eruption sent an ash cloud about 35 kilometers into the sky, and Typhoon Yunya, which struck at the same time, made the ash heavy and caused roofs to collapse. About 800 people died. The sulfur dioxide that it released lowered global temperatures by roughly half a degree Celsius for two years, and forced the closure of Clark Air Base.
target_summary: Mount Pinatubo erupted on June 15, 1991, killing about 800.

source: Mount Apo, standing 2,954 meters above sea level, is the highest mountain in the Philippines. This dormant volcano straddles the provinces of Davao del Sur, Davao City, and Cotabato, and it is part of a protected natural park that was declared a UNESCO World Heritage candidate. The mountain has solfataras, sulfur vents that release steam, and a crater lake called Lake Venado. It is home to endangered wildlife, including the Philippine eagle, and it is considered sacred by the Bagobo and other indigenous groups. Climbers need a permit and must hire local guides, and the climb usually takes two to four days, depending on the trail. Hikers must be well prepared because of sudden fog, cold temperatures, and slippery rocks.
target_summary: Mount Apo, 2,954 meters high, is the Philippines' highest peak.

source: The Philippines is one of the most linguistically diverse countries in the world, with more than 170 languages spoken across its islands. Filipino, which is based largely on Tagalog, and English are the two official languages, while the Constitution also recognizes regional languages as auxiliary official languages in their areas. Tagalog, Cebuano, Ilocano, Hiligaynon, and Waray are among the most widely spoken first languages. Cebuano alone is spoken by about one quarter of the population, mostly in the Visayas and Mindanao. Many Filipinos speak two or three languages and mix them in everyday conversation, a habit known as Taglish when Tagalog and English are combined. Language policy in schools encourages the use of the mother tongue in early grades.
target_summary: The Philippines has over 170 languages; Filipino and English are official.

source: Machine learning is a branch of artificial intelligence in which computers learn patterns from data instead of following rules written by programmers. In supervised learning, a model is trained on examples with known answers, such as photos labeled cat or dog, and then predicts labels for new photos. In unsupervised learning, the model looks for structure in data without labels, for example grouping customers with similar buying habits. To check that a model works on unseen data, developers usually split their dataset into training, validation, and test sets, with a common ratio being 80 percent for training and 20 percent for testing. A model that memorizes the training data but performs poorly on new data is said to be overfitting.
target_summary: Machine learning lets computers learn patterns from data instead of rules.

source: Staying hydrated is important because water makes up about 60 percent of the adult human body and is needed for nearly every function, from regulating temperature to carrying nutrients in the blood. Most adults need roughly two liters of fluid a day, but the exact amount depends on climate, physical activity, and body size. People who work outdoors in hot weather or exercise heavily may need considerably more. Early signs of dehydration include thirst, dark yellow urine, headache, and tiredness. A simple way to check hydration is to look at the color of urine, which should be pale yellow. Fruits and vegetables such as watermelon and cucumber also contribute a significant amount of water.
target_summary: Water makes 60 percent of the body; adults need two liters.

source: Intramuros, which means within the walls in Spanish, is the oldest district of Manila. Founded in 1571 by the Spanish conquistador Miguel Lopez de Legazpi, it served as the political, religious, and military center of Spanish rule for more than 300 years. The walled city is surrounded by stone fortifications up to eight meters thick and includes Fort Santiago, the Manila Cathedral, and San Agustin Church, which was built in 1607 and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. During the Battle of Manila in February 1945, most of Intramuros was destroyed by artillery and fires. Today, the Intramuros Administration restores buildings and welcomes tourists, who can ride horse-drawn carriages through its cobblestone streets.
target_summary: Intramuros, Manila's walled city, was founded in 1571 by Legazpi.
